newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber say Thais turn down RSS3 offers.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber say Thais turn down RSS3 offers.

text.p: The Thai government seems to have turned down offers for 7,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber while European buyers engaged in shortcovering for TSR20 grade rubber in the local market, dealers said on Friday.

"I doubt the Thai government will buy the rubber," a senior dealer for a trading house in Singapore said, adding the offers of 124.00-124.50 U.S. cents a kg was higher than the price Bangkok was willing to pay at 123.50 cents.
The Thai government, in a bid to support sagging rubber prices, has been engaged in buying RSS3 rubber in the market and recently bought 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 at 123.50 cents a kg.

In the local market, traders said some European trading houses picked up a few hundred tonnes of TSR20 rubber to cover their positions. "It's been very quiet. I think the tonnages are not going to be inspiring," one dealer said.
Lacklustre activity in Japan also depressed the market. "If you look at the Tokyo market, which we closely follow here, nothing moved," a trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 121.00-123.00 U.S. cents a kg from 122.00 cents. October/December TSR20 was seen at 118.50-120.50 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 119.25 cents.
